hints: Write the equation of the normal passing through $A(4, 3)$ in the form $y = mx + c$.
walkthrough:
Evaluate the gradient of the tangent at point $A(4, 3)$:
$$m_T = \left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=4} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{4}} = \frac{1}{2}$$

Calculate the gradient of the normal line:
$$m_N = -\frac{1}{m_T} = -\frac{1}{1/2} = -2$$

Write the equation of the normal line through $A(4, 3)$ in $y = mx + c$ form:
$$y - 3 = -2(x - 4) \implies y - 3 = -2x + 8 \implies y = -2x + 11$$

hints: At $A$, $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{2}$ and the rate of change of $x$ is $\frac{dx}{dt} = 3\text{ cm s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
Apply the chain rule connecting the rates of change:
$$\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{dy}{dx} \cdot \frac{dx}{dt}$$

Substitute the gradient $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{2}$ at $A$ and the rate $\frac{dx}{dt} = 3\text{ cm s}^{-1}$:
$$\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{1}{2} \times 3 = \frac{3}{2}\text{ cm s}^{-1} \quad (\text{or } 1.5\text{ cm s}^{-1})$$

hints: Along the normal line, the gradient is $\frac{dy}{dx} = -2$.
The $y$-coordinate is decreasing at $5\text{ units s}^{-1}$, so $\frac{dy}{dt} = -5$.
walkthrough:
Identify the gradient along the normal line:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = -2$$

Set the rate of decrease of the $y$-coordinate:
$$\frac{dy}{dt} = -5\text{ units s}^{-1}$$

Apply the chain rule to determine $\frac{dx}{dt}$:
$$\frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{\frac{dy}{dt}}{\frac{dy}{dx}} = \frac{-5}{-2} = \frac{5}{2}\text{ units s}^{-1} \quad (\text{or } 2.5\text{ units s}^{-1})$$
